newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea employers group aims for limited wage freeze.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea employers group aims for limited wage freeze.

text.p: A South Korean employers' group agreed on Tuesday that it will recommend to its money-losing members that they freeze wages in 1997 in line with a government belt-tightening scheme.

"Companies reporting a deficit or a fall in sales would be recommended to freeze wage levels for their workers next year, whether they are executives or grassroots workers," said an official at the Korea Employers' Federation.
"Wage increases should be supported by improving productivity," said the official. More than 4,000 companies were registered as members of the federation.
State television said the decision could face resistance from South Korea's often-militant labour groups.
In September, South Korea's 30 largest business groups agreed to freeze total spending on executive pay and benefits next year, according to the Federation of Korean Industries.
South Korea's Finance Ministry announced new measures last week to boost the sagging economy, including steep price cuts and easing of overseas borrowings for large companies.
Company profits are being slashed by plunging prices for South Korea's major exports such as semiconductors and steel products.
